name: Weather + trend gradient boosting

selection_details.rule: Lowest equal-year mean of 2019, 2020 and 2021 rolling-origin mean absolute errors

peak_lead_time.date_basis: Issue date to start of the peak observed week

interval_calibration.method: Empirical quantiles of log((actual+10)/(forecast+10)) from the selected model's validation folds

prospective.protocol: Retrospective evaluation of the fixed 2019–2021 selection and hyperparameters; refitted once a year on labels ending before that year's first assumed issue date. Later years are excluded from recipe selection. Revised workbook counts and immediate publication are assumed; these are not forecasts recorded in real time.

peak_lead_time.date_basis: Issue date to start of the peak observed week
Issue date to start of the peak observed week

live_forecast.note: Forecasts for weeks not yet reported. Each row uses only labels ending before its assumed issue date; publication delays are unknown. The range is the model's own 80% error spread from 2019–2021, not a guarantee.

weather_missingness.method: Share of prediction weeks with at least one missing weather lag supplied to the selected learned estimator. Its imputer uses training-set medians internally; observations and exported features remain missing. The four-week-average baseline does not use weather.

model_config.validation: Expanding four-week folds, 2019–2021, equal-year MAE selection
model_config.holdout: 2022 reused evaluation year; excluded from selection in this revision

current_forecast.reason: Recent official weekly labels passed the freshness gate.

limitations: 2022 was viewed in earlier revisions. This revision fixes selection using only 2019–2021, then evaluates once on 2022.
2023 onward is a retrospective evaluation of the fixed recipe, refitted once a year using earlier labels; it is not performance recorded in real time.
Labels after 2022 come from the official MOH/CDA yearly workbooks, which can be revised slightly after first publication.
Historical issue dates assume the preceding week's case total was available immediately; publication delays are not known.
Area priorities have no historical local outcome labels and no local forecast accuracy can be measured.
Feature contributions describe associations; Heat combines temperature and humidity.
High means above the pre-evaluation training distribution's upper third; it is not an official outbreak threshold.
Lead time is descriptive of one replay, not evidence that every outbreak can be predicted this far ahead.
